claim: Visual appeal ratings of web homepages correlated between 50 ms and 500 ms exposures, so first impressions of appeal form within about 50 ms (Lindgaard et al., 2006).
quote: visual appeal can be assessed within 50 ms, suggesting that web designers have about 50 ms to make a good first impression
title: Attention web designers: You have 50 milliseconds to make a good first impression!

claim: In a 1,530-participant study, webpage prototypicality correlated strongly with visual aesthetics, perceived pre-use usability and trustworthiness, and its direct effect on trustworthiness outweighed the indirect effects (Miniukovich and Figl, 2023).
quote: Notably, the direct effect of prototypicality on trustworthiness outweighed the indirect effects through aesthetics and usability.
title: The effect of prototypicality on webpage aesthetics, usability, and trustworthiness

claim: In an online survey of over 1,400 participants (2000), respondents reported a web site loses credibility when it has errors, technical problems or distracting advertisements.
quote: People reported that a Web site loses credibility when it has errors, technical problems, or distracting advertisements.
title: Elements that affect web credibility
publisher: CHI Conference Extended Abstracts on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI EA)

claim: Paintings actually made by AI were judged more positively on liking, beauty, profundity and worth when randomly labelled human-created than AI-created, with perceived effort and narrativity moderating the sensory-level label effects (Bellaiche et al., 2023).
quote: Study 1 found increased positive judgements for human- compared to AI-labelled art across all criteria.
title: Humans versus AI: whether and why we prefer human-created compared to AI-created artwork

claim: Raters could not tell AI and human texts apart in a blind test but favoured texts labelled Human Generated over AI Generated by a preference score above 30%, also when labels were swapped.
quote: While the raters could not differentiate the two types of texts in the blind test, they overwhelmingly favored content labeled as "Human Generated," over those labeled "AI Generated," by a preference score of over 30%.
title: Human Bias in the Face of AI: Examining Human Judgment Against Text Labeled as AI Generated
publisher: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL (Findings of ACL)

claim: Thirteen experiments found that actors who disclose AI usage are trusted less than those who do not, explained by reduced perceived legitimacy (Schilke and Reimann, 2025).
quote: Thirteen experiments consistently demonstrate that actors who disclose their AI usage are trusted less than those who do not.
title: The transparency dilemma: How AI disclosure erodes trust
publisher: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes

claim: In a 618-participant experiment, an AI-generated label significantly reduced perceived creator effort while a human-made label did not differ from no label (Lim et al., 2026).
quote: The AI-generated label significantly reduced perceived effort, whereas the human-made label did not differ from the unlabeled condition
title: Human-made vs. AI-generated: how provenance labels drive strategic curation via perceived effort

claim: Across three studies, consumers were less forgiving of AI-created misrepresentative ads than human-created ones because AI ads were perceived as involving less effort; strong brand reputation buffered the effect (2026).
quote: consumers are less forgiving of AI-created misrepresentative ads than human-created ones because AI ads are perceived as involving less effort
title: Forgiving the Algorithm? Consumer Responses to AI- vs. Human-Created Misrepresentative Ads

claim: Non-expert readers identified AI-generated poems with 46.6% accuracy (below chance) when authorship was undisclosed, and rated AI poems more favourably on rhythm and beauty (Porter and Machery, 2024).
quote: participants performed below chance levels in identifying AI-generated poems (46.6% accuracy
title: AI-generated poetry is indistinguishable from human-written poetry and is rated more favorably

claim: Labelling a vaping-prevention message as AI rather than human significantly changed evaluations, with a slight bias against AI-generated messages once the source was disclosed, without significantly altering message rankings.
quote: source disclosure (i.e., labeling the source of a message as AI vs. human) significantly impacted the evaluation of the messages but did not significantly alter message rankings
title: The effect of source disclosure on evaluation of AI-generated messages
publisher: Computers in Human Behavior Artificial Humans

claim: In two preregistered survey experiments (n = 7,579 Americans), all tested AI labels decreased belief in the presented claims, but labels stating only that content was AI-generated had little impact on stated likelihood of engaging.
quote: labels that simply informed participants that content was generated using AI tended to have little impact on respondents' stated likelihood of engaging with their assigned post
title: Labeling AI-generated media online

claim: In a 36-participant study, different users produced less semantically distinct ideas with ChatGPT than with an alternative tool, and felt less responsible for their ideas (Anderson et al., 2024).
quote: different users tended to produce less semantically distinct ideas with ChatGPT than with an alternative CST
title: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation

claim: Across 2,200 college admissions essays, each additional human-written essay added more new ideas than each additional GPT-4 essay, and prompt or parameter changes did not close the gap (Moon et al., 2025).
quote: Diversity gap widens with more essays, showing greater AI homogenization at scale.
title: Homogenizing effect of large language models (LLMs) on creative diversity: An empirical comparison of human and ChatGPT writing
publisher: Computers in Human Behavior Artificial Humans

claim: GPT-4 and LLaMA-3 stories contained plot elements echoed across many generations and across LLMs, while human-written plots were rarely recreated (Xu et al., PNAS 2025).
quote: LLM-generated stories often contain combinations of idiosyncratic plot elements echoed frequently across generations and across different LLMs
title: Echoes in AI: Quantifying lack of plot diversity in LLM outputs
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: A 2026 preprint argues that LLM web vibe coding can homogenise web designs, with frictionless generation exacerbating the risk; it is a sociotechnical risk analysis with case studies, not a measurement.
quote: We identify that the push for frictionless generation can exacerbate homogenization and its harms.
title: Interrogating Design Homogenization in Web Vibe Coding

claim: A meta-analysis of 72 studies found the uncanny valley effect, a negative affective reaction to human-looking artificial entities, had a large pooled effect size (Hedges g = 1.01) (Diel et al., 2021).
quote: the UV effect had a large effect size, Hedges’ g = 1.01 [0.80, 1.22]
title: A Meta-analysis of the Uncanny Valley's Independent and Dependent Variables

claim: Humans detect fake reviews no better than chance; learning four features (one-sidedness, exaggeration, personal selling style, generic descriptions) lowered trust in the reviews and purchase intentions (da Costa Filho et al., 2022).
quote: while computers can effectively detect fake reviews, humans are no more accurate than chance
title: Mind the fake reviews! Protecting consumers from deception through persuasion knowledge acquisition

claim: Human raters were significantly less accurate and consistent than a machine classifier at detecting GPT-2-generated fake product reviews (Salminen et al., 2021).
quote: human raters exhibit significantly lower accuracy and agreement than the tested algorithms
title: Creating and detecting fake reviews of online products
publisher: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
